name: translate-lite
desc: Free, open-source offline translator for Windows — text and documents via local models, markdown-safe. 100 MB portable, no cloud, MIT.
features: ✅ **Offline engine** — neural translation packs run locally, no API keys and no text leaving the machine
✅ **Document mode** — txt, Markdown and docx files translated with formatting and code blocks preserved
✅ **Batch queue** — a folder of files translated into one target language unattended
✅ **Glossary list** — names and terminology pinned so they survive translation untouched
✅ **Two-pane workspace** — source and target side by side with sentence-level highlight matching
✅ **Pack manager** — languages installed and removed from the settings shelf with disk sizes shown
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime bundled, language packs download separately, offline after that, MIT
compare: | Feature | **translate-lite** | Google Translate | DeepL | Argos CLI |
| Price | **Free, MIT** | Free web | Paid tiers | Free, OSS |
| Text stays local | **Yes** | No | No | Yes
| Markdown and code preservation | **Yes** | Partial | Partial | No |
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Browser | App or web | Python env
faqQ: offline translator for Windows that keeps documents private?
faqA: Online translators see every contract and manuscript pasted into them, and the offline tooling is a Python package with rough output. translate-lite runs NMT packs locally, preserves Markdown and code, and enforces a glossary. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, no account, and works with the network cable unplugged.
s1: Dark panes (#121418, teal #14B8A6): source document left with sentence 14 highlighted, translation right with matching highlight, language pair chip reading DE to EN.
s2: Batch queue: 12 files with per-file status and word counts, target language dropdown, glossary badge on, progress bar reading 7 of 12 done.
s3: Pack manager: fifteen language tiles with download sizes, three marked installed, glossary editor panel with six pinned terms, disk usage chip.
